description: IBCS two-tier column chart (CO 4.2, UN 4.1): AC/FC columns with the reference scenario (PY or PL) overlapped behind and offset left, absolute variance tier above on the SAME value scale, variance axis in the reference scenario's notation. Options: pinTier adds the relative variance as pins in a third tier on their own % scale (card 8), showBase false draws the variance tier alone.

fields.Period: text, category axis label (e.g. Jan); use YYYY-MM for periodLabel 'month' or 'short'; sort the visual by period ascending
fields.AC: measure, actual; BLANK for periods without actuals
fields.FC: measure, forecast; BLANK for periods with actuals (optional)
fields.PL: measure, plan/budget (needed when refScenario = 'PL'); any other code works the same way, e.g. BU: bind the field under that name and set refScenario = 'BU' (every code except PY gets the plan notation: outlined column, two-line axis)
fields.Polarity: optional measure: 1 higher is better, -1 lower is better, 0 neutral; else the polarity knob
fields.BU: measure, budget (refScenario or triangleScenario 'BU'); plan notation like PL
fields.YMax: optional measure, same value on every row: upper end of the base tier in the measures' unit (before unitDivisor); wins over the yMax knob
fields.VarMin: optional measure: lowest variance the tier must show (≤ 0); wins over varMin
fields.VarMax: optional measure: highest variance the tier must show (≥ 0); wins over varMax
fields.PinMin: optional measure (fraction, ≤ 0): lowest relative variance the pin tier must show; wins over pinMin
fields.PinMax: optional measure (fraction, ≥ 0): highest relative variance the pin tier must show; wins over pinMax
fields.PxPerUnit: optional measure, same value on every row: px per display unit for the page's scale group; wins over pxPerUnit
fields.ScaleBand: optional measure, same value on every row: scale band value in data units (before unitDivisor); wins over scaleBand
fields.Comment: optional text/number per row: comment number shown in a circle above that period (blank = none)

layout.rule: container height = fixedPx + Σ over tiers of ((hi − lo) × pxPerUnit + padHigh + padLow); measured with Vega-Lite 6.4.3 at ibcsFontSize 12; with varPxPerUnit the variance tier contributes (hi − lo) × varPxPerUnit instead (scale_layout.py: member tierPxPerUnit); with Comment markers add ibcsFontSize + 18 px to the base tier's padHigh; periodLabel 'month' with visible category labels uses fixedPxMonthLabels instead of fixedPx for the second label line (at ibcsFontSize 12); tiers with onlyIf count only when that knob is true (showBase false drops the base tier and its padHigh; pinTier true adds the pin tier at pinPxPerUnit px per percentage point); with pxPerUnit the space the data does not need stays ABOVE the top tier, so the tiers never drift apart when a filter shrinks the data; categoryLabelPx > 0 fixes the category-label band: the fixed height is then fixedPxNoCategoryLabels + categoryLabelPx (months and Total with the same categoryLabelPx share their baseline)

previewVariants.note: Three tiers in one view: ΔBU% pins above ΔBU above AC&FC vs BU; pins on their own % scale (pinShare of the base tier).
pxPerUnit 10 and pinPxPerUnit 2 in a container taller than the data needs: the spare space stays above the pin tier, the three tiers stay together.
pinMin -30% / pinMax +30%: the pin tier reserves this range whatever the data, so a Total or a second chart with the same values gets its pin axis at the same height.
PinMin/PinMax and VarMin/VarMax bound as fields (one union measure each): they win over the knobs, so the tiers keep the union range under any filter.
legendSide start with a scale band near the middle of the last (FC) column: the band label moves clear of the FC name.
showBase false: only the ΔPY tier, for stacking a second variance tier above a chart that already draws the base.
showBase false with pinTier: a ΔPL + ΔPL% pair without the base.
Tiny values under a fixed pxPerUnit: the base tier is a few px high, the end legend still keeps the names ibcsFontSize + 2 px apart.
The same with legendSide 'start': AC and the reference name left of the first column keep a minimum vertical gap.

ibcs.notes: Same unit, same scale (CH 4.1) means the same px per unit, not the same domain: give every chart of a scale group the same pxPerUnit (or the PxPerUnit field from one DAX measure) and size each visual's height to its own data (usermeta.ibcs.layout; scripts/scale_layout.py in the ibcs-power-bi skill computes it), so a chart with smaller values is shorter (CH 4.2). yMax, varMin, varMax only share a domain: use them for visuals of the same height that must show the same range, never to align a smaller chart with a larger one. A Total / extension column (e.g. the year next to its months) is a separate visual with periodType 'year'; when its values need another scale, mark it with a scaling indicator or a footnote. Same column width across visuals (e.g. the month chart and its total): set barPx. Values are drawn as delivered: bind scaled measures or set unitDivisor so labels never show raw values. Rows with a blank Period or no value in AC, FC, PY, PL, BU, refScenario or triangleScenario are dropped, even if constant scale measures are present; reference-only periods remain. The integrated reference legend names the first period with a nonblank reference value, including zero. periodLabel: auto preserves category labels unchanged; month formats YYYY-MM as Jan..Dec with the year below the first visible month of each year and a thin separator at subsequent year boundaries; short formats YYYY-MM as mm. Other category formats are left unchanged. When showCategoryLabels is false, year labels and year separators are hidden too. Rounded-zero rule: a variance that rounds to 0 at `decimals` is labelled 0 without sign and gets no impact colour. Scale band (CH 4.3): when charts of one unit must use different scales, set scaleBand (display units, e.g. 10) to the same round value in each of them: a light area from the axis to that value and a labelled line make the scales comparable. 0 = off. Comment markers (UN 2.4): bind Comment (e.g. a DAX SWITCH returning 1, 2 … for the periods the comments explain) and print the same numbers in circles in the comment text box; the marker sits above the value label, so keep ibcsTierGapPx large enough when a variance tier is stacked above. Variance-only tier (showBase false): only the variance axis, variance columns and labels and the tier label are drawn; stack it above a chart that shows the base, with showCategoryLabels false when the visual below shows them. Pin tier (pinTier true): ΔX% = (AC&FC − REF) / REF with the signed reference, N/A when REF is blank or 0, or negative while naOnNegativeRef is true; drawn as pins above the absolute variance tier in the same view, so base, ΔX and ΔX% always share the category axis and stay together when a filter changes the data (separate stacked visuals each anchor their own plot and drift apart). The pins have their own % scale: pinPxPerUnit px per percentage point (the same on every pin tier and pin chart of the page), else pinShare of the base tier. Outlier clipping (clipPct) exists only in pin-relative-variance. Integrated legend (legendSide, default 'end'): the scenario names sit right of the last column at their own marks (triangle tip, upper part of the reference column, middle of the AC/FC column), spread at least ibcsFontSize + 2 px apart and kept inside the base tier; a series of AC months followed by FC months is named AC&FC; the right padding (46 px) holds 'AC&FC'. legendSide 'start' keeps AC and the reference left of the first column and FC right of the last; the names left of the first column are spread at least ibcsFontSize + 2 px apart too, so tiny columns under a fixed pxPerUnit never stack them. Names are taken from the last row: a scenario without a value in the last period is not named. With legendSide 'end' the scale-band label sits left of the first column (the right end belongs to the legend names). Pin tiers of visuals side by side (months and Total) align only with the same pin range (like the Δ tier range) and the same pinPxPerUnit. Under filters fixed knobs are not enough (the months' tiers grow with the data): bind VarMin/VarMax/PinMin/PinMax on both visuals to union measures; the fields win over the knobs, like PxPerUnit. The Total's Δ tiers use the Total's own px per unit (its own scale, like its base; scale band and footnote), so the Δ union is taken in px: Var Max Months = VAR m = MAXX(ALLSELECTED('Date'[Month]), [Δ BU]) RETURN MAX(MAX(m, [Δ BU Year] * [PxPerUnit Total] / [PxPerUnit Months]), 0) and Var Max Total = [Var Max Months] * [PxPerUnit Months] / [PxPerUnit Total] (VarMin likewise with MINX/MIN): both tiers get the same height. The pins share one % scale (pinPxPerUnit) on both, so Pin Max = MAX(MAXX(ALLSELECTED('Date'[Month]), [Δ BU %]), [Δ BU % Year], 0) for both. Give months and Total the same visual top, height and categoryLabelPx, so their baselines and tiers sit at the same y. With legendSide 'start' the scale-band label stays at the right end above the line and moves clear of the FC name.

previewGroups.note: one scale group, pxPerUnit 20: container heights from scale_layout.py (244 and 148 px); the smaller entity gets a shorter visual, not a taller empty domain

params.name: refScenario
params.description: reference scenario (subtrahend): 'PY' (solid light) or a plan code such as 'PL' or 'BU' (any code except PY gets the plan notation: outlined column, two-line variance axis); the field of that name must be bound

params.name: decimals
params.description: decimals for value and absolute-variance labels (the token formats with this precision); IBCS: at most 3 digits in charts

params.name: polarity
params.description: used when the Polarity field is absent: 1, -1 or 0

params.name: periodType
params.description: year | quarter | month | week | day: category width per period type (UN 3.3)

params.name: periodLabel
params.description: auto = unchanged category labels; month = YYYY-MM as Jan..Dec with a second line naming the year under its first visible month and a thin year separator; short = YYYY-MM as mm. Other category formats stay unchanged; showCategoryLabels hides both label lines and year separators.

params.name: stepScale
params.description: screen scaling of the token category step; keep it identical on every page

params.name: barPx
params.description: column width in px; 0 = 2/3 of the category slot. Set the same value in every visual of one period type on a page (e.g. 2/3 of the month slot) so their columns have the same width

params.name: unitDivisor
params.description: divides every value before drawing and labelling: 1 = the measures are already scaled (preferred, e.g. a scaled measure or a Scale picker), 1000 = thousands, 1000000 = millions. The unit belongs in the title (UN 2.2), never as K/M suffixes

params.name: yMax
params.description: upper end of the base tier in display units (after unitDivisor); 0 = from the data. A shared DOMAIN, not a shared scale: same yMax gives the same px per unit only on visuals of the same height. For a same-unit scale group use pxPerUnit instead (CH 4.2: a chart with smaller values gets a shorter plot, never a taller empty domain). The larger of knob and data wins, so nothing is ever cut

params.name: varMin
params.description: lowest value of the variance tier (≤ 0); 0 = from the data

params.name: varMax
params.description: highest value of the variance tier (≥ 0); 0 = from the data

params.name: pxPerUnit
params.description: px per display unit (after unitDivisor) on the value axis; 0 = off. When set, the value domain is the plot extent ÷ pxPerUnit, anchored at the baseline, so values render at exactly this px per unit. The container must then be sized to the data (usermeta.ibcs.layout, scripts/scale_layout.py of the ibcs-power-bi skill): a chart with smaller values gets a smaller visual, never a larger empty domain (CH 4.1 + CH 4.2). If the container is too small, the data wins and the px per unit shrinks: nothing is cut

params.name: varPxPerUnit
params.description: px per display unit for the variance tier only; 0 = the same as pxPerUnit. Default for a Total with its own scale: leave 0 (its Δ tiers use the Total's scale, ibcs-composition) and align it by px extent (categoryLabelPx, VarMin/VarMax). Set it only for a page that footnotes the compromise of a Total Δ on the months' scale (needs pxPerUnit > 0). Labels still show the true variance.

params.name: triangleScenario
params.description: a third scenario drawn as a triangle at its value (e.g. 'PY' when refScenario is 'BU' or 'PL'); its field must exist; '' = none. PY solid light, AC solid dark, any other code outlined (plan notation)

params.name: showCategoryLabels
params.description: false hides the category labels, e.g. for a tier stacked directly above another visual that already shows them

params.name: categoryLabelPx
params.description: height of the category-label band in px (axis extent incl. label padding); 0 = from the labels. Give a Total next to month columns the months' value (e.g. 28 with periodLabel 'month' at font 12) so both baselines sit at the same y; scale_layout.py uses it in the fixed height

params.name: scaleBand
params.description: scale band (CH 4.3) in display units: a light area from the axis to this value and a labelled line, the same round value in every chart of the unit whose scales differ; 0 = off (field ScaleBand wins)

params.name: fcLabel
params.description: integrated-legend name of the hatched (forecast) columns: 'FC' for forecast months; 'AC&FC' on a Total / extension visual whose column is the year of actual plus forecast (bind that measure as FC so it is hatched)

params.name: legendSide
params.description: where the integrated scenario legend sits: 'end' = right of the last column, each name at its own mark (triangle, reference, AC/FC), spread so names never overlap; a series of AC then FC months is named AC&FC there; 'start' = AC and the reference left of the first column, FC right of the last (previous behaviour); the names left of the first column are spread the same way, so tiny columns never stack them

params.name: showBase
params.description: false draws only the variance tier: no base columns, value labels, scenario legend, triangles, comment markers, scale band or category axis line. Use it for a second variance tier (e.g. ΔPY above an AC vs BU chart that already shows ΔBU) so the base is not drawn twice; with pinTier the visual is a ΔX + ΔX% pair

params.name: pinTier
params.description: true adds the relative variance (ΔX% = (AC&FC − REF) / REF, signed reference) as pins in a third tier above the absolute variance tier, in the same view, so all tiers move together under filtering and share one category axis (CO 4.2). The pins have their own % scale (pinPxPerUnit)

params.name: pinPxPerUnit
params.description: px per percentage point of the pin tier; set the same value on every pin tier and pin-relative-variance chart of the page (one % scale). Needs pxPerUnit > 0; 0 (or pxPerUnit 0) = the pin tier gets pinShare of the base tier's extent

params.name: pinShare
params.description: without pinPxPerUnit: extent of the pin tier as a share of the base tier (of the variance tier with showBase false)

params.name: pinDecimals
params.description: decimals of the pin labels (percent)

params.name: pinMin
params.description: lowest relative variance the pin tier must show, as a fraction (-0.1 = -10%); 0 = from the data. Set the same pinMin/pinMax on every pin tier of a row of visuals (e.g. the months and their Total) so their pin axes sit at the same height

params.name: pinMax
params.description: highest relative variance the pin tier must show, as a fraction (0.15 = +15%); 0 = from the data

params.name: naOnNegativeRef
params.description: pin tier: N/A when the reference is negative (IBCS UN 4.1); a zero or blank reference is always N/A

params.name: ibcsLabelPad
params.description: label room, as a share of the largest value (pxPerUnit = 0)

params.name: ibcsTierGap
params.description: gap between the tiers, as a share of the largest value (pxPerUnit = 0)

params.name: ibcsLabelPx
params.description: label room in px beyond a bar end (pxPerUnit > 0 only; else ibcsLabelPad)

params.name: ibcsTierGapPx
params.description: gap between the tiers in px (pxPerUnit > 0 only; else ibcsTierGap)

params.name: tokBw
params.description: column width of the token layout; sizes the triangle so it stays clear of the neighbouring columns

params.name: bw
params.description: column width: 2/3 of the category slot, space 1/3; barPx gives every visual of one period type the same width

params.name: triPx
params.description: triangle height: token ratio × column width / bar thickness, clamped in px (geometry.triangleSizePx)

params.name: pinBw
params.description: pin tier: the token column width, so pins keep the size of pin-relative-variance

transform.filter: isValid(datum['AC']) || isValid(datum['FC']) || isValid(datum['PY']) || isValid(datum['PL']) || isValid(datum['BU']) || isValid(datum[refScenario]) || (triangleScenario != '' && isValid(datum[triangleScenario]))

transform.calculate: isValid(datum['AC']) ? datum['AC'] / unitDivisor : (isValid(datum['FC']) ? datum['FC'] / unitDivisor : null)
showBase ? max(datum._maxV, datum._maxR, isValid(datum._maxT) ? datum._maxT : 0, datum._kMax, datum._band, 0) : 0
showBase ? (datum._ppu > 0 ? ibcsTierGapPx / datum._ppu : datum._M * ibcsTierGap) + (datum._anyComment > 0 ? (datum._ppu > 0 ? (ibcsFontSize + 18) / datum._ppu : datum._M * 0.12) : 0) : 0
datum._ppu > 0 && pinPxPerUnit > 0 ? pinPxPerUnit / datum._ppu : pinShare * datum._span / max(datum._pHi - datum._pLo, 1)
datum._B + datum._dHi + datum._lp + datum._tgP + datum._lp - datum._pLo * datum._pk
!isValid(datum._p) || abs(datum._p) * 100 * pow(10, pinDecimals) < 0.5 ? null : datum._pol == 0 ? ibcsNeutral : (datum._p * datum._pol > 0 ? ibcsGood : ibcsBad)

datum._pOk ? (abs(datum._p) * 100 * pow(10, pinDecimals) < 0.5 ? format(0, '.' + pinDecimals + '%') : format(datum._p, replace(ibcsFmtRelVar, /[.][0-9]+/, '.' + pinDecimals))) : (isValid(datum._v) ? ibcsNA : '')
pinTier ? datum._P0 + datum._pHi * datum._pk + datum._lp : datum._B + datum._dHi + datum._lp
!isValid(datum._d) || abs(datum._d) * pow(10, decimals) < 0.5 ? null : datum._pol == 0 ? ibcsNeutral : (datum._d * datum._pol > 0 ? ibcsGood : ibcsBad)
isValid(datum._d) ? (abs(datum._d) * pow(10, decimals) < 0.5 ? format(0, replace(ibcsFmtAbs, /[.][0-9]+/, '.' + decimals)) : format(datum._d, replace(ibcsFmtVar, /[.][0-9]+/, '.' + decimals))) : ''

axis.labelExpr: periodLabel == 'auto' || !test(/^[0-9]{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$/, toString(datum.value)) ? datum.label : periodLabel == 'short' ? substring(datum.value, 5, 7) : periodLabel == 'month' ? [split('Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec', ' ')[toNumber(substring(datum.value, 5, 7)) - 1], indexof(domain('x'), datum.value) == 0 || substring(domain('x')[indexof(domain('x'), datum.value) - 1], 0, 4) != substring(datum.value, 0, 4) ? substring(datum.value, 0, 4) : ''] : datum.label

layer.description: invisible: keeps the top tier inside the y domain; with pxPerUnit the domain is the plot height ÷ pxPerUnit
year separator: thin assisting line before the first visible month of each subsequent year (periodLabel month only)

transform.filter: periodLabel == 'month' && showCategoryLabels && isValid(datum._periodYear) && datum._i > 1 && datum._periodYear != datum._previousYear

layer.description: selection (cross-filtering): assisting-area band behind every mark of the selected category; no mark is dimmed (a dimmed AC reads like PY)
scale band (CH 4.3): light area from the axis to the common value, with a labelled line; set the same value in every chart of the unit whose scale must differ
scale band line
category axis (base line), drawn before the columns so every mark is in front of it
variance axis = reference scenario: PY solid light thick line
variance axis = reference scenario: PL/BU two parallel lines (upper)
variance axis = reference scenario: PL/BU two parallel lines (lower)
AC -> FC separator (vertical assisting line at the first FC period)
reference scenario column (PY solid light / PL outlined), behind and offset left
white underlay so hatched FC columns hide the reference column behind them
AC solid dark / FC hatched (pbiPatternSVG), in front
third scenario (triangleScenario) as a right-pointing triangle left of the column pair, tip at its value; size clamped in px
value labels of the primary scenario only (UN 2.3), above the taller of the overlapped pair
numbered comment marker (UN 2.4, UN 5.1): circle with the number of the comment that explains this period, above its value label; the same number marks the comment text
comment marker number
variance columns: same width and same scale as the base columns; colour = impact (3 states), geometry = arithmetic sign; FC minuend hatched
variance labels outside, in the direction of the change

integrated start legend (legendSide 'start'): AC and the reference name left of the first column (AC at the upper part of its first column, the reference low at its first period with a value), the triangle scenario name left of the first triangle; spread in screen pixels like the end legend (gap ibcsFontSize + 2), so tiny columns under a fixed pxPerUnit never stack the names on top of each other, and kept inside the base tier

xOffset.expr: datum._lgKey == '_lgT' ? -bw / 2 - ibcsOffsetCol * bw - triPx - 3 : -bw / 2 - ibcsOffsetCol * bw - 3 - (triangleScenario != '' ? triPx + 2 : 0)

layer.description: integrated legend: FC right of the last forecast column (legendSide 'start')
tier label ΔPY / ΔPL left of the variance axis

integrated end legend (legendSide 'end'): scenario names right of the last column, each at its own mark (triangle tip, upper part of the reference column, middle of the AC/FC column), spread in screen pixels so they never overlap (gap ibcsFontSize + 2) and kept inside the base tier

scale band label: left of the first column with the end legend (the right end belongs to the names); with legendSide 'start' at the right end above the line, moved clear of the FC name (≥ ibcsFontSize + 2 px between centres)

transform.calculate: legendSide == 'end' ? 0 : (isValid(datum._fPx) && abs(datum._bPx - (ibcsFontSize / 2 + 2) - datum._fPx) < ibcsFontSize + 2 ? (datum._fPx < datum._bPx ? max(ibcsFontSize / 2 + 2, datum._fPx + ibcsFontSize + 2 - datum._bPx) : datum._fPx - ibcsFontSize - 2 - datum._bPx) : -(ibcsFontSize / 2 + 2))

layer.description: pin tier (pinTier): variance axis = reference scenario, PY solid light thick line
pin tier: PL/BU two parallel lines (upper)
pin tier: PL/BU two parallel lines (lower)
pin tier: pin body, thin, impact colour; geometry follows the arithmetic sign; own % scale
pin tier: white ground under hatched FC heads
pin tier: pin head in the minuend's notation (AC solid dark, FC hatched)
pin tier: labels outside the head in the direction of the change; N/A on the axis
pin tier: tier label ΔPY% / ΔPL% left of its axis
